drug_authority.value: Licensed physicians may prescribe drugs, including controlled substances, subject to statutory limits. For opioids, first-time prescriptions are limited to a 7-day supply for adults and 5-day supply for minors, with exceptions for acute conditions, chronic pain, cancer, and palliative care.
drug_authority.quote: When issuing a prescription for an opioid drug to an adult patient for the first time for outpatient use, a prescribing practitioner who is authorized to prescribe an opioid drug shall not issue a prescription for more than a seven-day supply of such drug

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates must have received the degree of doctor of medicine, osteopathic medicine or its equivalent, satisfy educational requirements specified in regulations, and either (i) successfully completed all components of a 'fifth pathway program' conducted by an American medical school accredited by the AMA or AOA, or (ii) received certification from the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG).
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: is a graduate of a medical school located outside the United States or Canada and has received the degree of doctor of medicine, osteopathic medicine or its equivalent and satisfies educational requirements specified in regulations adopted pursuant to this chapter and has either (i) successfully completed all components of a "fifth pathway program" conducted by an American medical school accredited by the American Medical Association or the American Osteopathic Association, or (ii) received certification from the Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates

pain_management_education_required.quote: risk management, including, but not limited to, prescribing controlled substances and pain management

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: First-time opioid prescriptions for adult outpatients are limited to a 7-day supply; for minors, a 5-day supply. Exceptions exist for acute medical conditions requiring more, chronic pain, cancer-associated pain, and palliative care, with documentation required.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: When issuing a prescription for an opioid drug to an adult patient for the first time for outpatient use, a prescribing practitioner who is authorized to prescribe an opioid drug shall not issue a prescription for more than a seven-day supply of such drug

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: The provisions of section 20-9(a) apply to any individual whose practice of medicine includes any ongoing, regular or contractual arrangement providing diagnostic or treatment services through electronic communications to persons in Connecticut, requiring licensure. Electronic radiographic image reporting also requires licensure for ongoing arrangements. Non-residents consulting irregularly with in-state licensed physicians or with medical schools for educational purposes are exempt.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: The provisions of subsection (a) of this section shall apply to any individual whose practice of medicine includes any ongoing, regular or contractual arrangement whereby, regardless of residency in this or any other state, he provides, through electronic communications or interstate commerce, diagnostic or treatment services, including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, slides or images, to any person located in this state.

telemedicine_license_available.quote: The provisions of subsection (a) of this section shall apply to any individual whose practice of medicine includes any ongoing, regular or contractual arrangement whereby, regardless of residency in this or any other state, he provides, through electronic communications or interstate commerce, diagnostic or treatment services, including primary diagnosis of pathology specimens, slides or images, to any person located in this state.

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: The Interstate Medical Licensure Compact is hereby enacted into law and entered into by the state of Connecticut with any and all states legally joining therein in accordance with its terms.

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: "Supervision" in hospital settings means the exercise by the supervising physician of oversight, control and direction of the services of a physician assistant.

physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.value: Physician assistants may, as delegated by the supervising physician: prescribe and administer drugs including controlled substances in schedule IV or V in all settings; renew prescriptions for controlled substances in schedule II, III, IV or V in all settings; prescribe and administer controlled substances in schedule II or III in all settings (with supervising physician documentation of approval); and prescribe and approve use of durable medical equipment.
physician_assistant_prescriptive_authori.quote: A physician assistant may, as delegated by the supervising physician within the scope of such physician's license, (I) prescribe and administer drugs, including controlled substances in schedule IV or V in all settings, (II) renew prescriptions for controlled substances in schedule II, III, IV or V in all settings, (III) prescribe and administer controlled substances in schedule II or III in all settings

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: A physician shall report to the department any disciplinary action similar to an action specified in subsection (a) of section 19a-17 taken against him by a duly authorized professional disciplinary agency of any other state, the District of Columbia, a United States possession or territory, or a foreign jurisdiction, within thirty days of such action.

hospital_privilege_action_reporting_requ.quote: Any health care facility licensed under section 19a-493 which terminates or restricts the staff membership or privileges of any physician shall, not later than fifteen days after the effective date of such action, notify the department of such action.

impaired_physician_program_authorized.quote: If the department determines that probable cause exists to issue a statement of charges, the entire record of such proceeding shall be public unless the department determines that the physician is an appropriate candidate for participation in an assistance program in accordance with the provisions of sections 19a-12a and 19a-12b.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: As part of an investigation of a petition filed pursuant to subsection (a) of section 20-13d, the Department of Public Health may order the physician to submit to a physical or mental examination, to be performed by a physician chosen from a list approved by the department.

investigational_drug_protection.quote: Notwithstanding the provisions of this chapter, the Department of Public Health or the Connecticut Medical Examining Board shall not revoke, fail to renew, suspend or take any disciplinary action against a physician based solely on the treating physician's recommendation to a patient regarding access to, or treatment with, an investigational drug, biological product or device, provided such recommendation is consistent with medical standards of care.
